title: Dominari: option grants, pre-announcement trading and the Trump sons' arrival
summary: The figures in the brief hold up. On Feb. 10, 2025, the day before the Trump sons' advisory roles were announced, Dominari granted CEO Anthony Hayes and president Kyle Wool fully vested options on 5M shares each (10M in all). The grant was struck at the $6.16 close, after a roughly 530-580% six-week run-up, and depended on a 10M-share plan increase that stockholders approved on April 1, 2025. The same day, Hayes, Wool and other insiders bought into the $3.47 private placement alongside the sons. Bloomberg reports about $66M of 2025 pay, a figure that includes grant-date option value. No source identifies who bought during the run-up, and no SEC, FINRA or Nasdaq inquiry, filed shareholder suit or lawmaker referral on the trading was found. Among the comparators, only Unusual Machines (documented) and SRM (single-source, 67% in two days) show a pre-announcement run-up. A new layer: Trump Organization executives Alan Garten, Lawrence Glick and Ron Lieberman are also Dominari shareholders, and Garten and Glick sit on a Yorkville SPAC board (C78).

sub_claims.statement: Hayes and Wool were granted 10M options on Feb. 10, 2025, the day before the Trump sons' advisory roles were announced.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (Dominari 8-K, 10-Q and FY2025 annual report, via search excerpts; sec.gov was blocked for direct fetch). The compensation committee granted a nonqualified option on 5,000,000 shares each to Wool and Hayes. The 10-Q describes the options as 'fully vested' and granted on Feb. 10, 2025. The exercise price was fair market value on the grant date, and the options expire after ten years (2/10/2035). The annual report's option table lists 5,000,000 options at a $6.16 exercise price for each executive, and the proxy shows a $30.8M disclosed value per grant (5M x $6.16). The options could not be exercised until stockholders approved a 10M-share increase in the 2022 plan reserve. Aggregator Form 4 listings date the reported awards to Apr. 16, 2025, after that approval. One aggregator's '10,000,000 options to Wool at $3.85' conflicts with the filings and is discarded. The announcement came on Feb. 11, so 'the day before' is accurate. Advisory agreements with the sons were also dated Feb. 10 (C39).

sub_claims.statement: The options were struck after the run-up, and their value depended on the post-announcement jump.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the prices; the paper-value arithmetic is inferred (our own calculation, which no source makes). Barron's put DOMH up 529% from $0.98 on Dec. 31, 2024 to $6.16 at the Feb. 10 close. The FT says about 580% in six weeks. The $6.16 strike is therefore the pre-announcement close, so the grant did not capture the January run-up. It did capture what followed: the stock rose as much as 84% on Feb. 11 (Bloomberg) and closed at about $13 on Feb. 13 (Axios). At $13 the 10M options had intrinsic value of about $68M (our arithmetic). DOMH ended 2025 just under $5 (C39), below the $6.16 strike, so at year end the options were out of the money (also our inference).

sub_claims.statement: Hayes, Wool and other insiders bought stock at $3.47 in the same placement as the Trump sons, on the day of the option grant.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (Form 4/13D via Investing.com and aggregator listings; Forbes; Barron's). On Feb. 10, 2025 (closing Feb. 12), Wool bought 288,184 shares plus 288,184 Series A warrants ($3.72 strike, Feb. 2030) and Series B warrants for a combined $3.47 per share, about $1M of personal funds. His 13D shows 2,200,769 shares beneficially owned, including 1,241,989 held by his spouse, Soo Yu. Investing.com separately reports Hayes buying in the placement, and an aggregator's Form 4 summary puts his direct holding at 975,007 shares afterwards (single-source). Forbes reports that the CEO, COO, president and four board members together bought 664,000 shares at $3.47. Barron's says the private sale was 2,436,587 shares, and the sons each invested about $1M. Dominari described the $13.5M deal as priced 'at the market under Nasdaq rules'. That price was about 44% below the $6.16 close on the day the options were struck. Our explanation, which no source states, is that the Nasdaq minimum price can use a five-day average, which lags a fast-rising stock. The SEC record shows no open-market buying by Hayes or Wool during the January run-up; their only reported buys are the Feb. 10 placement. This is unverified because Form 4s were not read directly.

sub_claims.statement: Stockholders approved the plan increase that made the options exercisable, with a record date after the insiders' and sons' Feb. 2025 share issuances.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the meeting facts (DEF 14A and 8-K via search excerpts); the voting-power observation is inferred. The special meeting on Apr. 1, 2025 had a Feb. 24, 2025 record date. It raised the 2022 plan reserve from 1,404,404 to 11,404,404 shares. A quorum of 6,027,100 shares (about 42% of eligible shares) attended, and the amendment passed 5,684,835 for, 321,884 against, 20,381 abstaining. Because the record date came after the Feb. 10-12 issuances, the sons (966,138 shares each per 13G) and Hayes and Wool (roughly 3.2M including Wool's spouse) could vote shares acquired that week. Together these come to about 5.1M, close to the 5.68M 'for' votes. That is our own observation: no source says how any of them voted, and the 13G share counts may include shares that were not entitled to vote. Proxy language confirmed that Hayes and Wool could not exercise unless the increase was approved.

sub_claims.statement: Hayes and Wool were paid about $66M for 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the totals (Bloomberg, Jan. 27, 2026, syndicated on Bloomberg Government); the breakdown is single-source. Bloomberg reports Hayes at about $34M and Wool at almost $32M for 2025. An aggregator gives Wool's breakdown as $500,000 salary, $11M cash bonus, $860,894 stock awards, $13.1M option awards and $6.2M non-equity incentive pay (about $31.8M). '$66M paid' therefore mixes cash with the accounting value of the Feb. 2025 options, which were under water at year end. In June 2025, Dominari amended both executives' employment agreements to drop their right to further stock grants in exchange for a cash bonus tied to net revenue (8-K). On Mar. 4, 2026, stockholders approved another 10M-share plan increase, of which the proxy contemplated 6M for special awards to Hayes and Wool. It also added an evergreen of up to 20% of outstanding shares each year from 2027 to 2032. Bloomberg ties the 2025 pay to deals with the Trump family.

sub_claims.statement: Who traded DOMH before the announcement is identified.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented that the trading was anomalous (FT, Forbes, TipRanks); no source identifies the buyers. Forbes says daily volume averaged about 1.2M shares from Dec. 30, 2024 through Feb. 10, 2025, against about 11,500 before. TipRanks gives under 2,000 rising to over 200,000. Law professor Adam Pritchard (Michigan), quoted by the FT, called the moves 'clearly unusual'. He noted that a board adviser may not face the same trading restrictions as a director. No reporting names a buyer, and no open-market purchase by the sons or by Dominari officers in January 2025 was found. Under the Barron's reading of the 13Gs, the sons stayed below 10% each, so they were not Section 16 insiders and did not file Form 4s (C39).

sub_claims.statement: SEC, FINRA or exchange inquiry, or shareholder suits, over the trading or the grants.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: absence of record, through Nov. 2026. No SEC, FINRA or Nasdaq inquiry into the pre-announcement trading was found, and Dominari's filings disclose none. On Oct. 27, 2025, Purcell & Lefkowitz LLP announced a 'shareholder investigation' into whether Dominari's directors breached fiduciary duties over unspecified 'recent corporate actions'. That is a plaintiff-firm solicitation, not a filed complaint, and no follow-up suit was found. Separate customer-complaint solicitations concern one Dominari Securities broker and are unrelated. The April 2025 Democratic senators' letter asking the SEC to probe insider trading concerned the tariff pause, not Dominari. The only official scrutiny of Dominari is the House China committee letter (Mar. 8, 2026) on Chinese IPOs, and the FINRA fine on Revere (C47).

sub_claims.statement: Trump Organization executives beyond the sons hold Dominari stock, and two of them also sit on a Yorkville SPAC board.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: the stakes are documented (the May 2025 S-3 resale prospectus as reported by Siegelman/NewsTRACS, plus Bloomberg via Raw Story, which reports three other Trump Organization executives holding shares). The SPAC overlap is our own cross-reference of two documented facts. The S-3 registers up to 13,940,546 shares for resale. Its selling stockholders include Don Jr., Eric, Alan Garten (Trump Org chief legal officer), Lawrence Glick (EVP Development) and Ronald Lieberman (EVP, Dominari director since Dec. 2024). Together they hold about 5.03M shares, about 20% of the stock after the offering, with Garten, Glick and Lieberman at about 8%. When and at what price Garten and Glick bought is not established. In C78, Garten and Glick are directors of Yorkville-controlled Texas Ventures Acquisition III. No source links the two roles.

sub_claims.statement: Wool's former firm Revere earned Dominari related-party underwriting revenue.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (a filing excerpt surfaced by an aggregator summary; not read directly). Dominari disclosed that Wool held a 30% equity interest in Revere Securities until May 2025, and that Dominari earned $5.8M in 2025 and $930,000 in 2024 from underwriting transactions in which Revere also participated. This connects to FINRA's October 2026 $800,000 fine on Revere for small-cap IPO AML failures (C47). FINRA does not name Wool, and no source says the fined deals overlap the Dominari co-underwritings.

sub_claims.statement: Unusual Machines had a similar pre-announcement run-up.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (FT via Yahoo/Telegraph syndication and TipRanks; NBC). UMAC 'almost tripled' (more than 220%) in the four weeks before Don Jr. was named adviser on Nov. 27, 2024. Average daily volume rose to 290,000 shares in the prior month, from 93,000 in March-October 2024. Osborne Clarke's Jeremy Summers said the pattern had 'the potential to involve insider dealing'. The companies did not respond. No regulatory inquiry was found. Dominari was later UMAC's placement agent (C39, C32).

sub_claims.statement: SRM Entertainment (Tron Inc.) had a pre-announcement run-up before the Dominari-placed Justin Sun deal.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (Protos). Protos reports that SRM shares rose 67% in the two trading days before the June 16, 2025 announcement. It found no public sign of how anyone could have known early. On the day, shares went from $1.70 to $2.25 within a minute of the premarket release and reached $6.70 within an hour. Dominari Securities was exclusive placement agent (C47). No options-volume data or inquiry was found.

sub_claims.statement: Thumzup and Gryphon (American Bitcoin's predecessor) had similar pre-announcement run-ups.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the announcement-day moves; no pre-announcement anomaly was reported for either. Thumzup was up about 167-267% year to date when Don Jr.'s 350,000-share stake was disclosed on July 9, 2025, after a Dominari-arranged $6M preferred placement. The stock then fell 14-17% on the day. No outlet flagged unusual trading beforehand. Gryphon jumped about 283-328% on the May 12, 2025 announcement of its all-stock merger with American Bitcoin (Benzinga premarket: about +304% to $2.10). Coverage gives no sign of a run-up in the preceding days. We did not check daily price data, so a small pre-move cannot be excluded.

corrections: The brief implies the options captured the pre-announcement run-up. They were struck at the $6.16 Feb. 10 close, after the ~530-580% rise, and their gain came from the post-announcement jump. They were not exercisable until stockholders approved the plan increase on Apr. 1, 2025.
'Executives were paid ~$66M' counts grant-date option value (e.g. about $13.1M of Wool's ~$32M, single-source) alongside cash. The Feb. 2025 options were under water at end-2025.
Thumzup and Gryphon show no reported pre-announcement run-up. Thumzup fell on its disclosure, and Gryphon's spike came on the announcement.
No SEC, FINRA or exchange inquiry and no filed shareholder suit was found. The only shareholder item is a plaintiff-firm 'investigation' notice (Oct. 2025).
denials_and_context: Dominari: it had 'no reason to believe that any of these people breached any duty, whether legal or fiduciary' and had no information about why investors bought before the announcement (FT/Forbes coverage, C39).
Dominari spokesman Brett Maas (May 2025): neither advisers nor investors had sold shares (C39).
Don Jr. bought Thumzup on his investment adviser's recommendation and has no other involvement with the company (Bloomberg, as reported by The Block).
A pre-announcement run-up is consistent with leaks, but also with momentum or speculative trading. No source shows that any named person traded on nonpublic information.

The options were priced at fair market value on the grant date and approved by stockholders. Grants at market price before a planned announcement are legal if disclosed, although governance experts criticize 'spring-loaded' timing (general point; no source applies that term to Dominari).
The companies (Dominari, Unusual Machines) did not respond to FT requests for comment on the trading.
sec.gov, panabee.com, quantisnow.com and equibles.com could not be resolved for direct fetch in this session. Filing details come from search-result excerpts and secondary summaries.
